people.role: Head of Hồng Lô Cốc since 930 (A028); the furnace that is said never to cool
people.appearance: A short, broad old man with a burn-glazed face and no eyebrows, who carries a bronze censer on his belt and warms his hands on it while he talks.
people.backstory: Đồng Hồng Lô was born in the valley in 760 to two of the founder's furnace-men, Fire-Wood alchemists who had followed Tiết Thừa Hỏa (tiet_thua_hoa) out of Thúy Vi. He was carrying coal in the kitchens at six. Tiết took him as her disciple at twelve because he would sit by a fire all night and not sleep. In 902 the Cold Ford War was fought along the coast to the east, and the furnace brewed its wound pills for no fee (N-hong_lo-02). In the winter of 929 the founder went down into the vent below Kê Quan Khoáng to bring up fire, and she did not come up (N-hong_lo-03). He became master in 930 and kept the furnace burning for nine years without letting it cool (A028). To do it he ran snow-melt through copper jackets around the furnace, which is where the valley's water half began. The habit became the Water Over Fire Canon, and it brews two batches in a season where Thúy Vi brews one. His best student was Viên Chước (vien_chuoc). In 1144 Viên lost the valley's year of ash money at the tables of Hàn Tân Thành, and Đồng sold his contract to Băng Tâm's head to cover it and called it theft. The valley knows. In 1145 he opened the gate to Water roots (N-hong_lo-04). In 1185 the isles smoked, and at 425 he sailed out with the boats to gather the ash before the rain did (A031). He has about sixty years left.
people.wants: To form his Nascent Soul over the Red Furnace before his years run out, as Úy Thanh Diễm did over the green one.
people.secret: The bill of sale he sealed in 1144 gives Băng Tâm one boat of ash at the 1144 price in every ten years. This season Viên Chước has come for a whole boat, and Đồng is making up the difference to the ash count from the fire jade he saved for his Nascent Soul pill. Phòng Tẫn Thủ sells it for him to the outside crews.

people.role: First elder; keeper of the snow jackets and author of the Snow Hearth Primer
people.appearance: A tall woman in a seal-skin coat over red felt, with frost on her sleeves and soot on her hands, who never raises her voice in the furnace hall.
people.backstory: Tần Tuyết Thán was born in the valley in 985. Her father fed the furnace, and her mother was a daughter of Nghiêu Phá Lãng (nghieu_pha_lang), the whale hunter who went out on the whale road in 884 and did not come back (V013). She was born with Fire and Water in almost equal measure. The founder's primer taught Fire roots only, so half her root went to waste. Đồng Hồng Lô (dong_hong_lo) took her as his disciple at fourteen and set her to the snow jackets, the copper sleeves of melt that keep the furnace from boiling over. She was the first to understand why they worked. She wrote down the last three layers of the Water Over Fire Canon, formed her core in 1120, and became first elder in 1140. In 1145 Đồng opened the gate to Water roots, and she wrote the Snow Hearth Primer for it in one winter (N-hong_lo-04). Since then the whale crews' children have come in through the kitchens, and the crews call her their elder. She keeps the sect's books and the ash ledger. Every morning she pours her gourd into the jackets herself.
people.wants: To see a Water root walk through the furnace hall's door as an inner disciple before she dies, which the rule forbids.
people.secret: She is writing a Water main method for the furnace hall. Her own share of this season's ash is paying for its test batches, and when it is done she means to put it before the council with a crew child already through its first layer.

people.role: The head's true disciple; the old Red Sun way
people.appearance: A lean young man with scorched forearms and a cinnabar-red robe he dyes himself, too bright for the valley.
people.backstory: A cook's son born in the kitchens, Ngụy Đan Chu tended Viên Chước's (vien_chuoc) furnace from the age of eight and learned more from him than from anyone. When Viên went to Băng Tâm in 1144, Đồng Hồng Lô (dong_hong_lo) took the boy as his true disciple. He means to be what Viên would have been. He thinks the snow jackets have made the Red Furnace timid, and he says so at council. He is the only disciple who still brews the old one-batch way. When the outside crews brought dice back in the ash rush of 1200 he took the table in the snow house, takes a coal's weight of every pot, and lends the outer boys their stakes against their ash shares.
people.wants: To be named heir of the Red Furnace and strip the snow jackets off it.
people.secret: He is cutting a Red Sun seal in the cellar to forge patents for the old one-batch way, and has Khổng Viêm Sinh (khong_viem_sinh) grind the cinnabar for the ink without saying what it is for.

people.exception: R2: admitted for a craft the sect hires (healing and herb-finding); a Wood root keeping Thanh Nang Đường's own method, never taught the lineage
people.appearance: A small grey woman with a green satchel across her chest, the only green thing in the valley.
people.backstory: Giải Bách Bộ was thirty-nine and the senior healer of Thanh Nang Đường when its last head, Thai Bạch Thược (thai_bach_thuoc), died in closed-door cultivation without naming an heir (V018). She led twenty-two healers north to Hồng Lô with their satchels. One of them, Dư Tục Đoạn (du_tuc_doan), twenty-one, walked the other way to Thúy Vi with a six-year-old. She runs the Satchel Hall, where herbs are brewed over spirit wood rather than the vent. She buys Lô Dã Hương's marten pups to find the herbs the tundra will not grow.
people.wants: To keep the Satchel Hall's healers members of the sect, not a hired craft.
people.secret: She hides a lame marten pup under her satchel table from the cooks, and has taught it to fetch her sleeping herbs.

people.role: Captain of the ash boats; an outer disciple for a hundred years
people.appearance: A huge man in oiled seal-skin with a harpoon of whale rib across his back and salt in his beard.
people.backstory: Great-grandson of Nghiêu Phá Lãng (nghieu_pha_lang), born among the crews' families at Bồ Diệp Thôn. His Fire is too thin for the furnace hall, so he has been an outer disciple for a hundred years and captain of the boats for sixty. In 1185, when the isles smoked for a month, he took the alchemists out to gather the ash before the rain (A031). That month, through the clear water of the smoking year, he saw his great-grandfather's boat on the warm reef off Kình Cốt point, its hull full of fire jade, and he has sworn to raise it. Since 1145 he has taught the harpoon inside the gate.
people.wants: To raise his great-grandfather's boat and its fire jade from the reef off Kình Cốt point.
people.secret: He has drawn the reef's marks on a whale-rib chart and is paying an outside crew from Hàn Tân Thành out of his own ash share to meet him there, without telling Nghiêu Lãng Hoa (nghieu_lang_hoa).

people.appearance: Remembered as a tall woman with singed brows and a coal-box always on her hip.
people.backstory: A disciple of Thúy Vi's first Furnace Master, Âu Dương Thanh Lô (au_duong_thanh_lo), who would not settle for green fire. In 650 she sailed to the volcanic isles with the sect's leave and the chart it had sealed in 565 (A022), and brought back a coal in a jade box. She lit it on the valley's vent and founded Hồng Lô Cốc (A024). Her journal says she first came to the vents looking for the fire of Cung Hỏa Vân (cung_hoa_van), who had vanished there in 640 (C013). In 929 the island coal died in a blizzard, and she went down after the vent's own fire.
